cards.headline: A 10-minute single posted as a teaser's follow-up
cards.snippet: In June 2012, ahead of his debut album Channel Orange, Frank Ocean put a short teaser video on his Tumblr account with a snippet of a new track. Later the same day he put the full song, "Pyramids", on his official SoundCloud account. Listeners who expected a brief trailer clip found that the track runs nearly 10 minutes. It became the album's second single, after "Thinkin Bout You".

cards.headline: A pimp, Cleopatra and real Los Angeles neighbors
cards.snippet: "Pyramids" tells of a pimp who falls in love with one of his workers, with Cleopatra woven into the story. Frank Ocean said in an interview that it came from his time living in Los Angeles, where pimps were among his neighbors. He described it as a fantasy built on that dynamic. He added that you can only write what you know to a point.
cards.context: Ocean explained the inspiration in an interview.

cards.headline: An intimate bath scene that quietly turns into a transaction
cards.snippet: The narrator is Cleopatra's ex-lover, or possibly a frequent john, per the annotation. He treats her as his own, though she may be a prostitute. The intimacy suggests he has won her back.
cards.context: One commenter says "you showed up after work I'm bathing your bod-" is the "best verse I've ever heard."
